headline: Colorado River Access and Territorial Prison Entry
reservation: Most historical sites and state parks in Yuma operate on a walk-in basis, but large groups for the Yuma Territorial Prison should contact the park in advance. During the peak winter visitor season, local RV resorts and campgrounds reach capacity, necessitating reservations months ahead of time. Check official state park sites for seasonal event registration.

days.title: Frontier History and Law

stops.name: Yuma Territorial Prison State Historic Park
stops.detail: Walk through the original cells and guard tower of the late 19th-century prison overlooking the river.

stops.name: Colorado River State Historic Park
stops.detail: Learn about the Yuma Quartermaster Depot's role in supplying army posts across the Southwest.

days.driving: Allow 10 minutes; these sites are located near the historic downtown core.
days.note: Early morning visits are recommended to avoid high midday desert temperatures.

days.title: Colorado River Recreation

stops.name: West Wetlands Park
stops.detail: Explore the restored riverfront habitats, burrowing owl mounded nests, and walking trails.

stops.name: Ocean-to-Ocean Bridge
stops.detail: Photograph the first highway bridge to span the lower Colorado River, a notable engineering landmark.

days.driving: Allow 15 minutes; parks are interconnected by local roads and bike paths.
days.note: River currents can be strong; adhere to all posted safety signage regarding water entry.

days.title: Desert Landscapes and Dunes

stops.name: Imperial Sand Dunes (Buttercup Area)
stops.detail: Witness the vast expanse of shifting sands used in many film productions.

stops.name: Mittry Lake Wildlife Area
stops.detail: Visit for birdwatching and photography in the marshes between the desert hills and the river.

days.driving: Allow 45–60 minutes for the drive to the dunes; conditions vary with wind and sand drift.
days.note: Imperial Sand Dunes require a permit for off-road vehicle use; check BLM guidelines before entering.

intel.title: Downtown and Parks
intel.text: Ample parking is available at the Territorial Prison and West Wetlands Park. Downtown street parking is generally accessible but monitor time limits near the historic Main Street district.

intel.title: Border Proximity Issues
intel.text: Cell phones may occasionally pick up towers from Mexico near the river, leading to potential roaming charges. Manually lock your carrier or use airplane mode if staying close to the international boundary.

intel.title: Desert Travel Prep
intel.text: Yuma is a major hub on I-8, but fuel options diminish rapidly when heading north toward the Kofa National Wildlife Refuge. Always carry extra water when traveling into the surrounding desert areas.

intel.title: Winter Peak Season
intel.text: The population of Yuma increases significantly between November and March. Expect longer wait times at popular restaurants and historical sites during these cooler months.

intel.title: Military Land Restrictions
intel.text: Yuma is surrounded by the Yuma Proving Ground and MCAS Yuma. Strictly obey all 'No Trespassing' and 'Range Closure' signs on desert tracks, as these indicate active military training zones.

plan.arrival: Fly into Yuma International (YUM) and pick up your vehicle; most major hotels and supply stores are located along 4th Avenue and 16th Street.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are fine for town sites, but a high-clearance 4WD is necessary for exploring Kofa or the deep sands of the Imperial Dunes.
plan.goldenHour: Gateway Park under the Ocean-to-Ocean Bridge for sunset colors reflecting off the Colorado River.
